questions.text: How does AI image analysis differ from the optical character recognition that has existed for decades?

options.text: They perform the same task, but AI image analysis is simply a faster version of it.
OCR extracts raw text from an image, while AI image analysis can also describe diagrams, explain the layout and organise the content into structured notes.
OCR interprets diagrams and explains their meaning, while AI image analysis only lists the words it detects.
OCR can read a photograph of a board, while AI image analysis works only on files created digitally.

questions.explanation: The lesson describes AI image analysis as content understanding rather than text recognition: from a single photograph it can read the text, describe the diagram and explain how the elements relate to each other.

questions.text: AI voice interaction is essentially the same thing as a text-to-speech tool reading content aloud.
questions.explanation: The lesson calls the two fundamentally different. Text-to-speech converts written text into audio, while AI voice interaction is a conversation in which the student can ask for a simpler explanation, an example or a comprehension check.

questions.text: Which statements about the practical limits of AI image analysis and voice interaction match what the lesson says?

options.text: A photograph taken from a distance, at an angle or in poor lighting produces less accurate results.
Handwritten text and complex diagrams can be misinterpreted, so descriptions may need correcting.
Schools need clear rules about classroom photography, because a photograph of the board may also capture classmates.
Once the photograph is clear, the AI's description of it can be treated as a guaranteed accurate transcript.
Spoken AI responses cause no disturbance in a shared classroom, so headphones are unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Image quality, misreading of handwriting and diagrams, and classroom privacy are the limitations the lesson names. It also warns that any AI description of visual content is an approximation, and that voice responses need headphones in a busy room.

questions.text: According to the lesson, what does a teacher actually need in order to start using AI with a student who has a visual impairment?

options.text: A smartphone with access to a mainstream AI tool, permission for the student to use it in lessons, and occasional review of the output.
A dedicated assistive technology device bought for the student and a specialist training course for the teacher.
A restructured lesson plan in which visual content is removed and replaced by spoken description.
A Braille transcription service that converts each photograph the student takes.

questions.explanation: The lesson states that no specialised assistive technology is required, because a smartphone with a modern AI platform already provides both image analysis and voice interaction. The adjustments asked of the teacher are awareness, permission and occasional oversight, not a redesign of their teaching.
